for: humanities/social-science PhD (communication studies / STS), international conference travel

funders.name: Ghana National Research Fund (GNRF)
funders.eligible_who: Researchers at Ghanaian tertiary and research institutions, across health, agriculture, technology and the sciences (scope for social science/communication studies not confirmed)
funders.amount_note: Not confirmed — the fund's own site gives no visible detail on grant sizes or an open international-conference-travel call.
funders.cycle: Unclear; as of 2024 reporting the fund was described as not yet fully operational, with the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) disbursing research support in the interim
funders.source_note: GNRF's own homepage gave only a title/tagline on fetch; no live call or amount could be verified. Treat as a category to watch, not a confirmed source — limited information.

funders.name: Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) research support
funders.eligible_who: Staff and postgraduate researchers at Ghanaian tertiary institutions, as an interim channel while GNRF becomes fully operational
funders.amount_note: Not confirmed — page not fetched in this run; GTEC's role here is inferred from third-party reporting, not a source quote
funders.source_note: Not independently verified on GTEC's own site in this run — flagged for a follow-up check rather than invented detail.

funders.note: Home institution: check the university's own graduate school or research office in Accra for an internal PhD conference-travel fund; specific to the institution and not tracked here.

funders.name: CODESRIA Small Grants Programme for Thesis Writing
funders.eligible_who: Doctoral students registered at African universities in the social sciences and humanities (Ghana qualifies as CODESRIA's home region)
funders.amount_note: Supports thesis writing rather than conference travel specifically; amount not confirmed on the page fetched — limited information
funders.requires: Registration at an African university, doctoral candidacy
funders.source_note: A real, long-running CODESRIA scheme (since 1988) but aimed at thesis writing, not international conference travel — relevant mainly as a fallback, not a dedicated travel grant.

funders.name: IAMCR Travel Grants (International Association for Media and Communication Research)
funders.eligible_who: Early-career (untenured) IAMCR members of ≥1 year, residing in low/middle-income countries (Ghana qualifies), first author of a paper accepted for full presentation at the IAMCR annual conference
funders.amount_note: Up to 18 grants, each max USD 2,000 (figures verified for the 2026 Galway cycle; amounts for future cycles not yet published)
funders.cycle: Annual, tied to each year's IAMCR conference; apply once that year's call opens
funders.requires: Paper acceptance confirmation from section/working-group head, IAMCR membership, full paper by the stated deadline
funders.source_note: Directly relevant field society for a communication-studies PhD; recurring annual scheme, but 2027 São Paulo-specific figures are not yet published.

funders.name: AoIR 2026 Access Grant (Association of Internet Researchers)
funders.eligible_who: AoIR members (or willing to join) with a paper, panel, roundtable or similar accepted at AoIR 2026; open to any career stage, with priority for regions less involved with AoIR previously
funders.amount_note: Up to 5 grants of up to USD 2,000 each, and up to 5 grants of USD 500 each, reimbursing travel or accommodation
funders.cycle: Tied to the AoIR2026 cycle; the 2026 deadline (10 July 2026) has already passed — relevant for a future AoIR edition, not this one
funders.requires: AoIR membership, accepted session at that year's AoIR conference
funders.source_note: Same scheme already recorded against corpus/opportunities/aoir-2026.json; kept here too since it recurs yearly for AoIR and is relevant to any Ghana-based internet/communication researcher.

funders.note: No current Ghana-specific bilateral trust or foundation dedicated to international conference travel (as opposed to degree scholarships) was found. DAAD's In-Country/In-Region Scholarship Programme funds Master's/PhD study within Sub-Saharan Africa, not conference travel, so it is not listed as a fit here.
No current destination-specific scheme (e.g. a host country's own funding for African early-career participants) was found for the destinations in this feed (Toronto, Jerez/Spain, Dakar, Bandung).
